correctness.rationale:
For \(3
mid n\), the recurrence kernel is trivial. For \(3\mid n\), the kernel is exactly the four three-periodic vectors, the image is exactly the two-constraint parity subspace, and each reachable output has four labeled predecessors. The target stabilizer \(\langle R^pangle\) acts either as fixed+three-cycle for \(3
mid p\), as identity for a reachable primitive \(p\)-block with \(3\mid p\), or as a nontrivial translation pairing for a nonreachable primitive block with reachable repetition. This reconstructs the 0/1/2/4 formula. Burnside counts reachable fixed outputs via \(H_n(d)\), and Möbius inversion counts primitive good blocks. Exhaustive independent comparison for all 1..18 ring sizes and arithmetic checks through 60 passed. Limits: finite experiments are corroboration, not the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Combining the polynomial image criterion with a necklace definition alone leaves unresolved the nontrivial stabilizer action: a four-point fiber can in principle yield 1, 2, 3 or 4 orbits. The new period-three kernel action forces only 2 or 4, and the period-block lift criterion determines exactly which. Möbius inversion then yields a new all-length exact census. No inspected source explicitly states a stronger formula from which all those quantitative conclusions follow.

evidence: Rule 105 is the output-complement of the Rule 150 local map, and output complementation preserves cyclic rotation orbits.
Krawczyk (2013) compares Rule 105 with Rule 150 but uses recursively refined state-neighborhood classes, not rotation classes.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Complementing all target bits translates the classification to Rule 105; it is acknowledged as equivalent, not a second finding. The cubic tap polynomial \(1+z+z^2\) is the algebraic form of the same map. Other additive Rule 90 has different labeled kernel size and ring-size singularity, so its own inverse-degree theorem neither contains nor implies this Rule 150 classification.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete all-ring-size invariant of an important elementary cellular automaton on rotationally unlabelled configurations: every target is classified, all inverse-degree classes have explicit integer enumerators, and a sharp generic four-parent law follows. The nontrivial period-three kernel/stabilizer mechanism explains collapse of four labeled parents into exactly two or four necklace parents. This is not a finite-table increment or a relabeling of the preceding Rule 90 theorem; Rule 150 is generically invertible on lengths coprime to three, whereas Rule 90 is never injective.
